source.title: Tensor Programs IV: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a different paper from the metadata title: it is headed “Tensor Programs VI: Feature Learning in Infinite-Depth Neural Networks,” not “Tensor Programs IV: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks.”
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own training-loss results for depth-scaled residual networks, but does not measure training classification error or test the specific conditions in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: CIFAR-10 training logloss and its changes with depth and hyperparameter scaling are relevant to training performance, but do not establish the claim’s classification-error outcomes. The study does not report CIFAR-100 or corrupted-label results.
record.test_reason: The study tests depthwise parametrization and hyperparameter transfer in residual MLPs and transformers. Its results do not test any of V1–V6: it reports training logloss rather than classification error, does not compare plain and residual convolutional networks, and does not compare the initialization, batch-normalization or curvature conditions those versions specify.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors identify Depth-µP as the unique optimal parametrization within their analyzed one-layer-block family, maximizing feature learning and feature diversity, and empirically demonstrate approximate depthwise hyperparameter transfer. They also report benefits from absolute-value activations and argue that deeper blocks face fundamental limitations within the considered parametrization family. Transformer transfer depends on training time.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes depth scaling and residual-network training loss, rather than the claim’s random-initialization classification-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcomes and optimal hyperparameters vary with depth scaling, block depth, activation, normalization, and training time.

fits_no_version.finding: For one-layer residual MLP blocks on CIFAR-10, Depth-µP approximately preserves the optimal learning-rate constant across sufficiently large depths while training logloss improves. Branch-only, unscaled and ODE parametrizations show depth-dependent shifts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint depth scaling of residual branch multipliers and optimizer updates can enable approximate depthwise hyperparameter transfer in one-layer residual MLP blocks.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-layer residual blocks show learning-rate shifts and worse matched-layer-count logloss than one-layer blocks; longer training closes the ReLU gap but not the absolute-value/LayerNorm gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depthwise hyperparameter transfer and training performance depend on residual block depth, activation, normalization and training duration.

fits_no_version.finding: Megatron transformers perform worse with greater depth initially but better later; optimal learning rates are approximately depth-invariant midway through training and scale approximately as inverse square-root depth at the end.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal learning-rate scaling across transformer depths can depend on training duration.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, 2021 (venue listed in metadata; supplied text cites ICML proceedings for related work but does not state this paper’s venue).
record.problems: The text reports logloss, not training classification error. Several depth comparisons are presented as plots without extractable numerical values in the supplied text. The general claims in Sections 7 and E are stated as claims or heuristics, and the paper notes omitted technical conditions or proofs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying rows identified. Several other plots report loss curves or feature-diversity statistics, but do not add a distinct explicit outcome relevant to the claim beyond the extracted settings.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, size effects, early stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut counterparts; special initialization of plain tanh networks and Fixup residual training.
Activation-matched initialization effects on plain-network learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and orthogonal convolution kernels.
Loss recovery above the initial linearized stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
Batch-normalization effects on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance, and matched Fixup comparisons without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied source is Tensor Programs VI: Feature Learning in Infinite-Depth Neural Networks, arXiv:2310.02244v5 (2023), not Tensor Programs IV (2021). The metadata's ICML 2021 venue belongs to the cited Tensor Programs IV paper. All row states remain cannot_determine relative to V1–V6; this does not deny the reported logloss and transfer effects.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size comparisons, and early stopping or regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum outcomes and the effect of student width.
Plain versus identity-shortcut networks and their training classification errors; no comparison of special initialization or normalization-free residual training as described.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons and the stated plain-network depth experiments.
Learning rates above stability thresholds, curvature or sharpness changes, and divergence outcomes.
Batch-normalization comparisons on the named architectures and accuracy-speed or learning-rate-tolerance measures; the paper’s LN experiments do not test these.

rows.subject: vanilla residual network with block depth 1
rows.operation_detail: Compared training logloss across depths under Depth-µP scaling on CIFAR-10.
rows.measure: Training logloss over 1000-step time slices; optimal learning rate across depth.
rows.value: The paper reports that Depth-µP “preserves the optimal learning rate while consistently improving the training loss as depth increases.”
rows.note: This reports training loss and learning-rate transfer, not classification error.
rows.check: An evaluation of the study's Depth-µP method, outside V1–V6. The subject is a residual MLP with frozen input/output layers, not a convolutional network. Learning-rate transfer is approximate: Section 10.2 reports mild shifts at small depths and concentration near 10^-3 from depth 64. Retain only as an out-of-version result.

rows.subject: vanilla residual network with block depth 1
rows.operation_detail: Compared training logloss across depths when only the residual branch multiplier was scaled, without learning-rate scaling.
rows.measure: Training logloss over 1000-step time slices; optimal learning rate across depth.
rows.value: The paper reports that the optimal learning rate “shifts significantly” with depth.
rows.note: No training classification error is reported.
rows.check: A comparator in the study's method evaluation, outside V1–V6. The learning-rate shift measures hyperparameter transfer, not a stability threshold or training classification error. Input/output layers are frozen.

rows.subject: vanilla residual network with block depth 1
rows.operation_detail: Compared training logloss across depths under standard parametrization without depth scaling.
rows.measure: Training logloss over 1000-step time slices; optimal learning rate across depth.
rows.value: The paper reports a “significant shift” in optimal learning rate as depth grows; even choosing the optimal rate at each depth, performance degrades when depth is very large.
rows.note: The reported outcome is training logloss/performance, not classification error.
rows.check: A comparator in the study's method evaluation, outside V1–V6. Add that Figure 20 attributes large-depth failure to numerical issues; Figure 10 caps displayed logloss at 1 for depths 512 and 1024, so those horizontal lines are not measured loss values. These are residual MLPs, without the plain-versus-residual convolutional comparison required by V3.

rows.subject: residual network with block depth 1
rows.operation_detail: Measured training logloss and optimal learning rate across depths under ODE parametrization.
rows.measure: Training logloss over 1000-step time slices; optimal learning rate across depth.
rows.value: The paper reports that the learning rate “exhibits a significant shift with depth.”
rows.note: The paper describes this as a feature-learning limit with sub-optimal hyperparameter transfer; it does not report classification error.
rows.check: An out-of-version parametrization comparison. ODE scaling changes branch multipliers and learning rates; it does not compare activation-matched initializations in plain networks or learning rates against an initial curvature threshold. Input/output layers are frozen.

rows.subject: vanilla residual network with block depth 1
rows.operation_detail: Compared training logloss across depths with LayerNorm under Depth-µP and branch-only scaling.

conditions.value: LayerNorm applied to x^(l−1) before multiplication by W^l

rows.measure: Training logloss over a 1000-step time slice; optimal learning rate across depth.
rows.value: The paper reports that Depth-µP preserves the optimal learning rate while training loss improves with depth; branch-only scaling has a significant optimal-learning-rate shift.
rows.note: LayerNorm is tested, but the reported measure is logloss and the comparison is not the batch-normalization claim in V6.
rows.check: An out-of-version method comparison. LayerNorm is not batch normalization, and the comparison varies depth scaling rather than adding versus removing normalization. Split Depth-µP and branch-only scaling into separate rows if retaining this result.

rows.subject: residual network with block depth 2
rows.operation_detail: Compared training logloss across depths for block depth 2 under Depth-µP parametrization.
rows.measure: Training logloss and optimal learning rate across depth.
rows.value: The paper reports a significant learning-rate shift; block-depth-2 experiments do not show learning-rate transfer.
rows.note: The text says these results might indicate adjustments are needed as block depth increases.
rows.check: An out-of-version evaluation of extending the proposed scaling to two-layer blocks. Section 9 explicitly reserves the name Depth-µP for block depth 1; describe this condition as α = γ = 1/2 scaling. Figure 21 uses the Figure 10 setup, including width 256.

rows.subject: residual network with block depth 2
rows.operation_detail: Compared minimum training logloss for block depth 1 and 2 at matched total layer count.
rows.measure: Minimum training logloss over block multiplier and learning rate.
rows.value: Block depth 2 does worse at 11000 steps but “can catch up” after longer training.
rows.note: This is loss/performance evidence, not a comparison of classification error.
rows.check: An out-of-version comparison of residual block architectures, matched for total layers and parameter count. It does not compare plain versus residual networks. Split the early deficit and later catch-up into separate time conditions; remove '1/1' from numbers_found because it is not an outcome value.

rows.subject: residual network with block depth 2
rows.operation_detail: Compared minimum training logloss for block depth 1 and 2 at matched total layer count.
rows.measure: Minimum training logloss over block multiplier and learning rate.
rows.value: Block depth 2 does significantly worse; training longer does not close the gap.
rows.note: This does not test whether identity shortcuts prevent training classification error from worsening.
rows.check: An out-of-version comparison of residual block architectures with absolute-value activation and LayerNorm. The persistent logloss gap does not establish failure of identity shortcuts in the batch-normalized convolutional networks specified by V3.

rows.subject: Megatron transformer trained on Common Crawl
rows.operation_detail: Compared training logloss and learning-rate trends across transformer depth.

conditions.value: cosine decay with 500 warmup steps; sequence length 4096; batch size 256; approximately 4B tokens per run
initial, middle, and end of training

rows.measure: Training logloss and optimal learning-rate scaling with depth.
rows.value: The paper reports deeper models do worse initially but eventually do better; optimal learning-rate trends differ between the middle and end of training.
rows.note: The study reports pretraining logloss, not classification error.
rows.check: An out-of-version transformer pretraining result. Split initial versus later depth effects and middle versus final learning-rate trends into distinct rows if retained. Figure 16 also distinguishes optimal learning-rate scaling from maximum viable learning-rate scaling; neither is measured against a curvature-derived stability threshold.
